scenarios.name: recent, well-provenanced context is usable first
scenarios.note: The baseline. Everything known, nothing missing. If this family fails for a client, the integration point is wrong before any policy question arises.

signal.title: Current release documentation
signal.content: Documentation for the release currently in production.

scenarios.name: known-stale context is demoted and disclosed, not blocked
scenarios.note: READ THIS ONE CAREFULLY BEFORE ADAPTING IT. safe_for_agent_handoff is true for a 2019 document, and that is correct. Its age is known and it is labelled use_as_background, so an agent receiving it has been told what it is. The state this engine blocks is UNKNOWN, not OLD - compare SW-03, which is newer in every respect except that its date could not be established, and is blocked. A client who reads handoff-safe as 'current' will misread their own evidence.

signal.title: Release notes for a superseded version
signal.content: Release notes describing a version that has since been superseded.

scenarios.name: context whose date cannot be established is held for verification
scenarios.note: Strong content, complete retrieval, unknown publication date. This is the family most often missing from a client's own test set, and the one that most often explains a production incident.

signal.title: Integration guide with no publication date
signal.content: An integration guide whose publication date could not be established.

scenarios.name: weak provenance lowers confidence and withholds handoff
scenarios.note: No source type, no retrieval timestamp. Retrieval succeeded and the content reads fine, which is exactly why this family is worth encoding: nothing about the text signals the weakness.

signal.title: Page with minimal provenance metadata
signal.content: A page retrieved without source type or retrieval timestamp.

scenarios.name: failed retrieval is excluded and can never pass through
scenarios.note: The contractual floor. A failed fetch must never be treated as usable context, whatever its content looks like. If only one family survives adaptation for a given client, keep this one.
